```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  prompt = FALSE
)
library(readPBOC)

release_snapshot <- data.frame(
  release_id = c("fixture-release-1", "fixture-release-2", "fixture-release-3"),
  language = c("en", "en", "zh"),
  category = c("fixture", "fixture", "fixture"),
  title = c(
    "Synthetic release fixture A",
    "Synthetic release fixture B",
    "Synthetic release fixture C"
  ),
  published_at = as.Date(c("2026-01-15", "2026-02-15", "2026-02-20")),
  url = paste0("https://example.invalid/readPBOC/release-", 1:3, ".html"),
  source_url = "https://example.invalid/readPBOC/releases.html",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
class(release_snapshot) <- c("pboc_release_index", class(release_snapshot))

resource_snapshot <- data.frame(
  asset_id = c("fixture/asset-a", "fixture/asset-b", "fixture/asset-c"),
  revision_id = c("fixture-r1", "fixture-r1", "fixture-r1"),
  year = c(2026L, 2026L, 2026L),
  language = c("en", "en", "zh"),
  section_id = c("fixture", "fixture", "fixture"),
  section = "Synthetic fixture section",
  item = c("Synthetic table A", "Synthetic table B", "Synthetic table C"),
  item_zh = NA_character_,
  item_en = c("Synthetic table A", "Synthetic table B", "Synthetic table C"),
  period = NA_character_,
  format = "xlsx",
  published_at = as.Date(c("2026-01-15", "2026-02-15", "2026-02-20")),
  url = paste0("https://example.invalid/readPBOC/asset-", 1:3, ".xlsx"),
  source_url = "https://example.invalid/readPBOC/catalog.html",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
class(resource_snapshot) <- c("pboc_resource_index", class(resource_snapshot))
```

PBOC publishes both data attachments and statistical statements. A reproducible
workflow treats the release index and the attachment catalog as separate
inventories: releases describe statements and publication dates, while catalog
rows identify files and revisions. The offline records in this article are
author-created structural fixtures under the package license. They contain no
PBOC product data and only demonstrate the shape and control flow; the guarded
live examples are the route for current official records.

## Work with a release index

The offline fixture is a small `pboc_release_index` data frame with `release_id`,
`language`, `category`, `title`, `published_at`, `url`, and `source_url`.

```{r release-snapshot}
stopifnot(inherits(release_snapshot, "pboc_release_index"))

english <- release_snapshot[release_snapshot$language == "en", , drop = FALSE]
english <- english[order(english$published_at, decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
english[c("release_id", "category", "title", "published_at")][seq_len(min(5L, nrow(english))), ]
```

For a current index, use
`pboc_releases()`
with a narrow category and page first. The live call is guarded so this
vignette remains deterministic on CRAN and offline machines:

```{r live-releases, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  releases <- pboc_releases(
    language = "en",
    category = "financial_statistics",
    pages = 1L
  )
  head(releases)
}
```

`language = "both"` combines independent Chinese and English indexes; it does
not imply that every statement exists in both languages. `pages = "all"`
traverses the page count reported by the source and can be substantially more
expensive than a single page.

To read the full text and attachment links for one row, use
`pboc_read_release()`.
It returns a `pboc_release` list containing `release_id`, `language`,
`category`, `title`, `published_at`, `text`, `paragraphs`, `attachments`, and
`url`. The live operation is deliberately limited to an interactive session:

```{r live-release-text, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  releases <- pboc_releases(
    language = "en",
    category = "financial_statistics",
    pages = 1L
  )
  if (nrow(releases)) {
    statement <- pboc_read_release(releases[1L, , drop = FALSE])
    c(
      title = statement$title,
      published_at = as.character(statement$published_at),
      paragraphs = length(statement$paragraphs),
      attachments = nrow(statement$attachments)
    )
  }
}
```

## Save a catalog snapshot

`pboc_snapshot()`
writes a catalog to a CSV path. It is an explicit side effect, so this example
uses a temporary directory. The structural fixture below has the same catalog
columns but uses reserved `example.invalid` URLs and synthetic labels; it is
not an official resource index.

```{r snapshot}
catalog <- resource_snapshot[seq_len(min(3L, nrow(resource_snapshot))), , drop = FALSE]
snapshot_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "readPBOC-vignette-snapshots")
dir.create(snapshot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
snapshot_path <- file.path(snapshot_dir, "catalog.csv")

pboc_snapshot(catalog, snapshot_path)
stopifnot(file.exists(snapshot_path))
identical(pboc_revisions(snapshot_path, catalog)$status, rep("unchanged", nrow(catalog)))
```

The function returns `path` invisibly. The CSV is suitable for keeping beside
an extraction run; it does not modify the package or create a global cache.

## Compare two snapshots

`pboc_revisions()`
matches rows by `asset_id` and compares their current revision metadata. It
returns a tibble with `asset_id`, `status`, previous/current revision IDs, and
previous/current URLs. The four statuses are:

* `unchanged`: the asset and revision are present in both snapshots;
* `revised`: the same asset has a different latest revision;
* `new`: the asset appears only in the current snapshot; and
* `removed`: the asset appeared only in the previous snapshot.

The following tiny data frames are synthetic control inputs that make each
classification visible without contacting the PBOC site. They use the same
columns as real catalog snapshots; they are not PBOC observations.

```{r revision-statuses}
previous <- data.frame(
  asset_id = c("same", "changed", "removed"),
  revision_id = c("r1", "r1", "r1"),
  url = paste0("https://example.invalid/", c("same", "old", "removed"), ".xlsx"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
current <- data.frame(
  asset_id = c("same", "changed", "new"),
  revision_id = c("r1", "r2", "r1"),
  url = paste0("https://example.invalid/", c("same", "newer", "new"), ".xlsx"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

changes <- pboc_revisions(previous, current)
changes[c("asset_id", "status", "previous_revision", "current_revision")]
```

When a revised file must be retained, use
`pboc_download()`
with the catalog row and an explicit destination directory. It names files
with the attachment/revision identifier, records URL/checksum/size/retrieval
time in a manifest, and leaves an existing revision alone unless
`overwrite = TRUE`. Downloading is intentionally not run in this vignette;
the operation writes files and requires an available official URL.

```{r live-download, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  destination <- file.path(tempdir(), "readPBOC-downloads")
  live_catalog <- pboc_catalog(
    year = 2026,
    language = "zh",
    section = "money",
    formats = c("xlsx", "xls")
  )
  if (nrow(live_catalog)) {
    pboc_download(live_catalog[1L, , drop = FALSE], destination)
  }
}
```

This explicit split—catalog metadata, snapshot, comparison, then optional
download—makes reruns auditable without depending on a hidden persistent
cache.
